history.rationale: V437 (V507 in full-length Nipah G) is a validated m102.4 escape site where the isoleucine sidechain sterically clashes with the antibody while preserving ephrin-B2/B3 binding.
V437I exhibits strong structural compatibility with near-WT stability and solid predicted escape capability.
Truncation of the hydrophobic valine sidechain at the m102.4 interface weakens antibody affinity while maintaining head-domain integrity.
V437A has moderate escape but lower structural compatibility compared to V437I.
D485 (D555 in full-length Nipah G) is a key contact with m102.4 heavy chain CDRs; neutral substitution disrupts electrostatic complementarity without disrupting receptor binding.
D485N shows the highest predicted immune escape score and favorable positive structural compatibility delta, making it the top candidate.
Extending the carboxylate sidechain alters local interface geometry with m102.4, providing escape while retaining receptor-binding viability.
D485E offers solid escape but is less structurally favored than D485N.
Eliminating the acidic sidechain abolishes critical polar/salt-bridge contacts with m102.4 paratope.
D485A displays strong escape potential, though D485N remains structurally preferable.
Removes the hydroxyl group participating in potential hydrogen bonding with m102.4 while conserving the aromatic scaffold critical for ephrin receptor engagement.
Y438F has excellent structural compatibility but the lowest escape score among the pool.
Located adjacent to D485 in the antibody footprint; alanine substitution reduces polar contact area with m102.4.
T486A exhibits moderate escape but penalized structural compatibility.
Introduces negative charge at the epitope periphery that can induce electrostatic repulsion with m102.4 while maintaining backbone conformation.
N487D combines robust structural compatibility with good predicted immune escape potential.
Adds moderate steric bulk to the loop backbone at the m102.4 contact surface to reduce antibody binding efficiency.
G436A severely destabilizes the backbone structure with a very poor ProteinMPNN log-odds score.
